headline: Hold the previous character out of the heap
statement: Rearrange all characters of s so no adjacent characters are equal. Return any valid rearrangement, or the empty string if none exists. Every original character must appear with exactly its original multiplicity.
intuition: Choose the available character with the most copies left, but hold the just-used character out of the choices for the next position. After choosing a different character, make the previous one available again. A heap helps choose the most frequent available character each time.
approach: Reject if a character count exceeds (len(s)+1)//2.
Heapify negative frequencies and repeatedly choose the most frequent available character.
After choosing, return the previously held character to the heap and hold the new one if copies remain.
correctness: The count bound is necessary because each repeated letter needs other letters as separators. It also establishes a scheduling invariant: with m remaining copies, the held previous letter has at most floor(m/2), and every available letter has at most ceil(m/2). Choosing a maximum available count and consuming one copy maintains these bounds for m-1. For odd m, the only possible count above the new available bound is the unique largest count and it is consumed; for even m, the available bound stays unchanged. The new held count meets its stricter bound and the old held letter becomes available. Hence the heap cannot become empty with copies remaining: that would put all copies in a held count exceeding floor(m/2). Every selection differs from its predecessor and consumes one copy, so the schedule finishes as a full valid rearrangement.
bruteForce: Try all permutations and inspect adjacent pairs, costing factorial time and producing many identical arrangements.

complexity.explanation: a is the number of distinct letters, at most 26; the heap stores counts and the output stores n letters.

pitfalls: A valid answer may differ from the shown reference output.
Do not reinsert the current letter before the next selection.
Returning a valid prefix is insufficient: all characters are required.
